div.div: A message with no visible state is the bug users report as "it didn't send". Render sending in a subdued style, and never let a failure look identical to a success.

Rendered instantly with a client id. The idempotency key is
this same id, so a retry cannot create a duplicate.

div.div:
Reconcile by client id, not by position. Order by the server
sequence — client clocks disagree and cannot be trusted.

div.div:
Messages 1042–1045 arrived while the socket was down.
Nothing errors. The conversation is simply missing four
messages and nobody is told.

div.div:
GET /messages?after=1041 on reconnect, then replay the
outbox. Idempotency keys make the replay safe even if the
server already received some of it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 511px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The socket is a day of work; reconnect, resume-from-cursor, idempotent replay and message ordering are the quarter. Every one of those is a follow-up question, and "resume from now" is the wrong answer to all of them — it loses messages silently, which is the worst failure a chat app can have.
